job.title: Health & Safety Advisor - Esperance
job.description:
This is an opportunity to join a WA organisation with an established, positive safety culture and excellent working relationships between the Safety team and Operations.

Safety is seen as a shared responsibility, with the team working alongside operational leaders and frontline employees to find practical solutions, manage risk and continually improve the way work is done.

Based in beautiful Esperance, this permanent opportunity offers the chance to make a meaningful contribution across diverse regional operations, backed by a supportive team and genuine commitment to safety and wellbeing.

This is a hands-on role for a safety professional who enjoys getting out into the business, building trust and helping people make good decisions. You will have the opportunity to influence safety outcomes, strengthen critical risk management and contribute to initiatives that make a real difference.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Partnering with operational leaders and frontline teams to strengthen safety ownership, accountability and positive safety behaviours.
  • Providing practical guidance on safety management systems, policies, procedures, hazard management and legislative compliance.
  • Supporting the critical risk program and monitoring the effectiveness of key controls.
  • Leading and supporting incident investigations using ICAM methodology, with a focus on meaningful corrective actions and learning.
  • Conducting workplace inspections and audits, identifying opportunities to improve safety and reduce risk.
  • Reviewing safety data and performance trends to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Contributing to safety improvement projects across geographically dispersed operations.
  • Working collaboratively with internal stakeholders to support health, wellbeing and injury prevention initiatives.
About You
You are a credible, approachable Health & Safety professional who understands that effective safety is built through relationships, engagement and practical action.

You enjoy working with operational teams, can influence without simply relying on authority, and know how to balance legislative requirements with the realities of getting the job done safely.

You will ideally bring:
  • A WHS qualification or equivalent, or significant relevant industry experience.
  • Experience in a high-risk operational environment such as utilities, mining, construction, engineering or a similar industry.
  • Strong communication, coaching and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Experience supporting and improving Safety Management Systems.
  • Sound knowledge of risk management, hazard identification, incident investigation and legislative compliance.
  • Experience conducting audits, inspections and workplace investigations.
Most importantly, you bring a collaborative mindset, sound judgement and a genuine commitment to helping people work safely.

Why Consider This Opportunity? A positive safety culture: Join an organisation where Safety and Operations work together constructively, with strong working relationships and a shared commitment to achieving good outcomes.

A supportive team: Work alongside a trusted, high-performing Safety team that values collaboration and practical contribution.

A role with influence: Build relationships across the business and help drive improvements that have a tangible impact on people, operations and regional communities.

A regional lifestyle: Enjoy living in Esperance, with its spectacular coastline, beaches and outdoor lifestyle, while building a rewarding career.

A package designed to support you: The remuneration package includes salary plus superannuation, a housing allowance, a location allowance and relocation support.

Work-life balance: This is a permanent Monday to Friday position with no regular weekend work, allowing you to enjoy life outside work.

Interested in Finding Out More? If you are an experienced safety professional looking for a role where relationships matter, collaboration is genuine and you can make a positive difference, I would love to hear from you.

Contact Suzi Johnson at The Safe Step by emailing your CV to sjohnson@thesafestep.com.au, or click Apply to submit your application.

job.title: Health & Safety Systems and Assurance Specialist
job.description:
Sydney | Permanent | National Scope

About Them
Our client is a highly successful Australian market leader with a long standing history and a reputation for operational excellence. Employing thousands of people across a diverse portfolio of businesses, they continue to invest in their people, systems and health and safety capability to support sustainable growth.
As part of a well regarded national health and safety team, this newly focused specialist role will play an important part in strengthening health and safety systems, governance and assurance across the organisation.

About the Role
Reporting to the Systems & Governance Manager, the Health & Safety Systems & Assurance Specialist will lead the ongoing development, implementation and improvement of the organisation's WHS Management System and health and safety assurance framework. 
This is a hands on technical role for someone who enjoys making safety systems clear, practical and effective. You will work closely with health and safety, operational, risk, audit and other key stakeholders to ensure WHS requirements are well designed, understood and effectively implemented across the business. 
A significant part of the role will also focus on assurance, including shaping the annual audit and assurance program, reviewing the effectiveness of risk controls and supporting improvements in how health and safety performance is monitored and reported. 

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for:
  • Leading the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the WHS Management System
  • Developing clear and practical WHS documentation aligned with legislative requirements, Codes of Practice and relevant industry standards
  • Maintaining the WHS system review program and supporting consultation on new and changing requirements
  • Monitoring legislative and industry changes and translating these into practical business requirements
  • Leading the development and implementation of the health and safety assurance plan
  • Establishing annual audit and assurance activities informed by risk profiles and WHS performance
  • Leading internal WHS audits and verification activities where required
  • Reviewing the effectiveness of health and safety risk controls, including critical risk controls
  • Supporting operational teams in the practical application of WHS system and compliance requirements.
About You
We are looking for an experienced health and safety professional with strong technical capability across WHS management systems, risk and assurance.
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience developing, writing and implementing WHS management systems
  • Strong knowledge of WHS risk management and assurance, including assurance frameworks and risk reviews
  • Experience with audit and verification activities and an understanding of risk control effectiveness
  • Excellent technical writing skills with the ability to make complex requirements clear and practical
  • The ability to interpret data and apply insights within an operational environment
  • Experience or strong capability across WHS technology, data and analytics
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to coach and build WHS capability
  • A relevant qualification in safety, risk or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
  • Lead Auditor qualifications would be highly regarded.
Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful systems and assurance work across a large and diverse operational organisation. Rather than simply maintaining an established system, you will have the opportunity to influence how WHS requirements are structured, applied, assured and continuously improved across the business.
The role will suit someone who enjoys getting into the detail of systems and assurance, but can also step back and understand how those systems need to work in a practical operational environment.

If you are an experienced WHS systems, governance or assurance professional looking for a technically interesting role with broad organisational reach, we would welcome a application or a confidential discussion.

job.title: HSE Business Partner
job.description:
The Organisation
An established Australian organisation operating across transport, fleet and essential services, with a strong focus on operational performance, continuous improvement and responsible business practices. With a geographically diverse workforce and operations spanning multiple locations, the organisation has a strong track record in safety, supported by established processes, systems and frameworks that provide a solid foundation for continued improvement.

As the business continues to evolve, an opportunity has arisen for an experienced HSE Business Partner to join the team in Queensland. This is an opportunity to work within a well-established safety framework, partnering with operational leaders and frontline teams to build on existing strengths, strengthen safety leadership and deliver meaningful improvements across a diverse, high-risk operational environment.

The Role
This is a hands-on, operationally focused role where you will partner with leaders across transport, fleet and field-based operations to further strengthen an already established safety culture.

Working within existing HSE systems, processes and frameworks, you will support the consistent application of safety standards while identifying opportunities to enhance risk management and operational outcomes. Working closely with the State leadership team and broader HSE function, you will provide practical advice, coach leaders and help translate business strategy into meaningful action.

With established foundations already in place, the focus is on collaboration, continuous improvement and ensuring safety practices remain effective, consistent and relevant to the realities of day-to-day operations.
Additionally, you will:
  • Build trusted relationships with operational leaders and frontline teams, providing practical coaching and guidance to strengthen safety ownership and accountability.
  • Partner with State leadership to implement HSE strategies, initiatives and improvement plans aligned with operational priorities.
  • Provide expert advice on safety risks associated with transport, fleet, mobile plant and field-based activities.
  • Support incident investigations, identify underlying causes and drive the implementation of effective corrective and preventative actions.
  • Monitor safety performance, analyse trends and identify opportunities to further strengthen existing systems and controls.
  • Deliver targeted safety initiatives, training and coaching to build leadership capability and workforce engagement.
About Success
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in a Health, Safety and Environment role within transport, fleet, logistics, construction or another high-risk operational environment.
  • The ability to build strong relationships and influence leaders at all levels, including where you do not have direct authority.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder engagement and coaching skills.
  • Experience supporting incident investigations, implementing corrective actions and monitoring safety performance.
  • Sound knowledge of WHS legislation, risk management principles and safety management systems.
  • Relevant WHS qualifications, ideally at Diploma level or above.
  • Able to travel locally in the Sunshine Coast area and into FNQ.
About Applying
If you are an experienced HSE professional who enjoys partnering with operations, building on established safety practices and making a tangible difference to safety outcomes, we would welcome your application.
Click Apply for this job below to apply.

For specific questions about this opportunity, please contact Suzi Johnson at sjohnson@thesafestep.com.au.

job.title: Group Risk and Retail Protections Manager
job.description:
About Them
Our client is one of Australia's largest and most successful specialty retail groups, with a diverse portfolio of well-recognised consumer brands operating across the country.  Serving millions of customers each year through an extensive store network of specialty brands, and growing digital channels, the business has built a strong reputation for delivering quality products, exceptional customer experiences, and trusted brands.
  
With a long history of success, the organisation continues to invest in innovation, technology, and operational excellence to support its next phase of growth. Its collaborative and high-performing culture encourages fresh thinking, continuous improvement, and strong leadership, creating an environment where people are empowered to make a meaningful impact.
  
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Group Risk & Retail Protection Manager to lead the organisation's enterprise risk, retail protection and asset protection strategy.  As the business continues to evolve, this role presents an outstanding opportunity to join a high-performing leadership team and make a genuine impact. This is a rare opportunity to join a dynamic organisation at an exciting point in its evolution, influence strategy, build strong stakeholder relationships, and contribute to the ongoing success.
  
About the Role
This leadership role will partner closely with the executive team to reduce retail loss, strengthen operational discipline and embed practical risk management across the business. This is a commercially focused role where success will be measured by tangible improvements in shrink, loss prevention, risk management, and business performance and continuity.
  
Leading a specialist team, you will develop and deliver an integrated risk and retail protection strategy that protects people, property and assets while supporting informed commercial decision-making.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading the risk and retail protection function across a large retail network.
  • Driving initiatives to reduce shrink, theft, fraud and total retail loss.
  • Strengthening operational controls, governance and accountability for risk across the business.
  • Leading enterprise risk management, business continuity and crisis preparedness.
  • Partnering with Property, Operations, Finance and Safety to improve physical security, asset protection and operational resilience.
  • Leveraging data, analytics and technology to identify trends, improve reporting and support better business decisions.
  • Presenting risk and performance reporting to Executive, Board and Audit & Risk Committees.
  • Building a high-performing team and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and commercial risk management.
About You
You are an experienced leader with a strong background in retail risk, asset protection, or enterprise risk (in a retail operating environment).  You have a proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and translate risk management into measurable commercial outcomes.
  
You will bring:
  • Senior experience in retail risk, loss prevention, asset protection or retail protection
  • Strong knowledge of store operations.
  • Experience with internal and external theft investigations.
  • Strong understanding of audits, compliance and operational controls.
  • Experience using data to influence operational decisions
  • Leadership of experienced specialist teams.
  • Exposure to enterprise risk, insurance or safety would be advantageous
  • Exceptional leadership, stakeholder engagement and change management capability.
  • A strategic, collaborative approach with a focus on delivering practical business outcomes.
This is an outstanding opportunity to influence organisational performance, protect enterprise value and shape the future direction of risk and retail protection within a dynamic retail environment.

How to Apply
Click the 'Apply Now' to register your interest.

Contact
Cate Ingham

job.title: Health, Safety and Wellbeing Director Systems and Enablement
job.description:
About the team
The Health, Safety & Wellbeing (HSW) team plays a critical role in enabling safe, healthy and sustainable ways of working across the University. Through listening, learning and a commitment to continuous improvement, HSW promotes consistent best practice, frameworks and standards across all faculties and business areas. Together, the team helps shape a culture where health, safety and wellbeing are embedded into everyday work, supporting organisational excellence and long-term success.

About the opportunity
The HSW Director Systems and Enablement is a senior University leadership role. In this position, you will be accountable for setting and driving the strategic direction of the University’s HSW systems, governance, assurance, reporting, and digital enablement functions.
Operating at a senior strategic level with influence extending to University Executive and Senate, the Director shapes a proactive agenda, provides trusted advice to senior leaders, and ensures sustained organisational focus on strategic priorities, risk management, and performance. The role plays a critical leadership function in embedding a cohesive and forward-looking approach to health, safety and wellbeing risks across the institution.

Your key responsibilities will be to:
  • lead the design and development of HSW Systems and Enablement function strategic objectives and goals for the University
  • team leadership and budget management
  • set and evolve the HSW Systems and Enablement operating model, ensuring clarity of roles, service offerings, and integration across systems, governance, assurance, and reporting functions
  • set and evolve the governance and reporting framework for the HSW function
  • lead the University wide assurance/audit program
  • provide strategic oversight and direction for HSW systems and digital enablement and continuous improvement
  • lead the University’s HSW Program Management activities.
This role will suit a contemporary HSW leader who combines strong systems and governance capability with the ability to set direction and lead digital and technology enabled change, while bringing people with them through complex organisational change.
  
About you
  • graduate degree/ professional qualifications or equivalent experience in a WHS or related discipline
  • extensive experience within Work Health and Safety field with a demonstrated experience of relevant legislation and policies
  • demonstrated leadership in developing an effective and sustainable safety culture and conceptualising, developing and implementing practical compliance and safety programs
  • extensive leadership experience leading multi-disciplinary Work Health and Safety specialist professionals within large, complex and highly regulated organisations
  • demonstrated experience in applying H&S Safety Management strategies in complex environments
  • advanced knowledge of Risk Management practices and the application of government legislation, codes of practice and Australian standards
  • advanced knowledge of relevant Australian Safety Standards as well as relevant Safe Work Australia, SafeWork NSW and Workcover publications
  • extensive experience with the development of HSMS systems and provision of technical supporting tools.
Sponsorship / work rights for Australia
Please note: You must have unrestricted work rights in Australia for the duration of this employment to apply. Visa sponsorship is not available for this appointment.

How to apply
The Safe Step is assisting the University of Sydney with this appointment. Applications (including a cover letter, CV, and any additional supporting documentation) can be submitted via the Apply button at the top of the page. For further information and a confidential conversation about the role please contact Stephen Coldicutt on scoldicutt@thesafestep.com.au or 02 8256 2529.

Pre-employment checks and declarations
Your employment is conditional upon the successful completion of all pre-employment or background checks required for the role in terms satisfactory to the University.  Also, to meet the University’s obligations under the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Eliminate Gender-Based Violence you will be asked to declare if you have been investigated for, or found to engaged in, sexual harm or gender-based violence in the course of previous employment or in a legal process. If you do not meet these conditions, the University may take any necessary step, including the termination of your employment.

job.title: HSE Advisor
job.description:

environment, builds strong relationships on site and takes a proactive approach to keeping people safe and building their capability an awareness around good safety culture.

job.title: Senior Safety Management System Specialist
job.description:
Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Safety Management Systems Specialist to join their specialised team on a 12 month Fixed Term Contract.

This is a corporate role for a technically strong safety professional who understands how safety works in the field and can translate complex legislative and operational requirements into clear, practical and easy to use documentation.  

You will play a key role in simplifying and strengthening the organisation’s Safety Management System, ensuring procedures, standards and supporting tools focus on the controls that matter most and can be readily understood and applied by frontline teams.  There will be a lot of work around discovery, decluttering, and simplification. 

Key Responsibilities:
  • Review, develop and simplify Safety Management System documentation, procedures, standards and guidelines
  • Translate legislative requirements, critical risks and critical controls into practical, easy to follow documentation
  • Engage with operational teams to understand how work is performed and ensure documentation reflects real world requirements
  • Facilitate risk assessments and identify gaps, improvement opportunities and areas of non-compliance
  • Lead stakeholder workshops, consultation and reviews to support continuous improvement of the Safety Management System
  • Develop and maintain supporting tools, resources and controlled documentation
  • Test and validate procedures in the field to ensure they are practical, effective and fit for purpose
  • Promote system awareness through training, presentations, inductions and communication materials
  • Partner with operational leaders and stakeholders to embed effective safety practices across the business
Position Skills and Qualifications:
  • Bachelor's degree in Safety, Environment, Business Administration, Management or a related discipline
  • 10+ years' experience developing and improving Safety Management Systems, Asset Management Systems or similar
  • Strong approach to writing, with the ability to simplify complex safety requirements into clear, concise documentation
  • Experience reviewing and improving procedures, standards, risk assessments and safe systems of work
  • Strong operational safety background, with the ability to engage directly with frontline teams and understand how work is performed in practice
  • Experience leading projects, managing change and supporting the implementation of revised systems and processes
  • Project Management, Business Process Mapping or Lead Auditor qualifications will be highly regarded
Join the Team:
This is an excellent opportunity to take on a 12 month Fixed Term Contract where you can genuinely influence how safety information is developed, communicated and applied across a large, complex organisation.

You will play a key role in simplifying existing documentation, strengthening critical risk controls and ensuring safety procedures are practical, accessible and meaningful for the people using them in the field.

If you enjoy turning complex safety requirements into straightforward solutions that make a real difference to operational safety, this role offers an opportunity to deliver lasting improvements.

Apply Now: To seize this exciting opportunity, submit your resume to sjohnson@thesafestep.com.au

job.title: National Technical Lead | Workers Compensation Self Insurance
job.description:
Sydney | Initial 6 month contract | National remit

An opportunity has become available for an experienced workers compensation professional to join a large, complex national organisation as National Technical Lead, Workers Compensation Self Insurance.
This is a specialist technical role focused on the governance, assurance and ongoing maintenance of self insurance licences across multiple Australian jurisdictions. It is not a claims management or case management position.
Working within an established national workers compensation function, you will take responsibility for a significant component of the organisation's self insurance regulatory programme, ensuring licences remain compliant and regulatory, audit and assurance obligations are effectively managed.

The Role
Working alongside an established national technical lead, you will:
  • Manage ongoing self insurance licence requirements across multiple Australian jurisdictions
  • Coordinate regulatory reporting, licence renewals and statutory submissions
  • Support and lead self insurance audits and regulatory reviews
  • Manage audit findings, corrective actions and associated assurance activities
  • Build effective working relationships with state and territory workers compensation regulators
  • Monitor regulatory and legislative changes and assess their impact on existing requirements
  • Provide specialist technical advice on self insurance, workers compensation legislation and regulatory compliance
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders and external claims administration partners
  • Maintain appropriate governance documentation, standards and technical frameworks
The role has responsibility across different Australian self insurance jurisdictions and includes regulatory licensing, statutory reporting, assurance audits, corrective action programmes and technical advisory responsibilities. 

About You
We are particularly interested in candidates who bring:
  • Strong, practical experience within a self insured workers compensation environment
  • Experience maintaining self insurance licences and working directly with regulators
  • Strong understanding of regulatory governance, assurance and audit requirements
  • Experience across multiple Australian workers compensation jurisdictions, ideally including NSW and other East Coast jurisdictions
  • Experience completing or supporting formal self insurance audits
  • The ability to interpret complex legislative and regulatory requirements and apply them in practice
  • Experience within a large, complex or national organisation
  • Strong technical writing and stakeholder management capability
  • A practical, hands on approach and the ability to quickly understand an established operating environment
The Opportunity
This is an initial 6 month contract opportunity, with potential for a longer term opportunity depending on the future structure of the broader team.
You will be joining a mature and established national function, so this is not a transformation brief. The priority is someone who can quickly understand the existing framework, take ownership and provide genuine technical depth across the self insurance portfolio.
For someone with strong self insurance expertise who enjoys the technical, regulatory and assurance side of workers compensation, this represents an opportunity to operate across a significant and complex national portfolio.

job.title: National Contractor Safety Lead
job.description:
The Organisation
As an ASX listed industry leader with operations across Australia, this organisation delivers essential services through a diverse operational network and contractor workforce. Safety is a core business priority, with significant investment being made in systems, governance and capability to support operational excellence and effective risk management.
 
About the Opportunity
This is not a traditional safety leadership role. We are seeking a contractor management specialist with deep expertise in contractor governance, assurance and compliance across large, operationally complex environments.
Working as part of a national HSE team, you will be responsible for leading and continuously improving the organisation's contractor management framework. You will partner with operational leaders across a diverse national footprint to strengthen contractor safety performance, improve assurance activities and drive consistent contractor management standards.

This role will suit someone who has spent a significant part of their career building, implementing or governing contractor management programs within sectors such as infrastructure, utilities, transport, resources, industrial services, construction, logistics or other contractor intensive environments.

What you will be doing
  • Lead the ongoing development and implementation of the Contractor Management Framework
  • Drive contractor prequalification, onboarding, assurance and compliance programs
  • Conduct contractor audits, reviews and verification activities
  • Support operational leaders to effectively manage contractor related risks
  • Strengthen contractor safety capability and performance across the business
  • Analyse contractor performance data and identify improvement opportunities
  • Participate in major incident investigations involving contractors
  • Ensure contractor activities meet legislative, governance and business requirements
What we are looking for
This role requires someone who is genuinely recognised for their contractor management expertise. You may currently be working in a contractor management, contractor assurance, contractor governance, contractor safety or critical risk role and have extensive experience managing complex contractor workforces across multiple sites.

You will likely bring:
  • Extensive contractor management experience within large, high risk or operationally intensive environments
  • Strong knowledge of contractor assurance, governance and compliance frameworks
  • Experience managing contractor onboarding, verification, performance monitoring and audits
  • A deep understanding of contractor related risk management and critical controls
  • The ability to influence operational leaders and drive accountability
  • Strong working knowledge of Australian WHS legislation and contractor obligations
Why This Role Is Different
Many organisations talk about contractor management as part of a broader safety role. In this position, contractor management is the role. You will be the recognised subject matter expert, helping shape how contractor risks are managed across a large and geographically dispersed operation while influencing the standards, systems and behaviours that support safe contractor performance nationwide.

Apply
If you have led contractor management programs within complex operational environments and are looking to influence contractor safety performance at scale, we would welcome a confidential discussion.

job.title: Safety Risk Specialist
job.description:
Join a well established national organisation where safety, risk management and operational excellence are receiving significant investment and leadership attention.

job.description:

This is an opportunity to join an established resource recovery and waste management operation in South Western Sydney, where environmental compliance, safety and operational excellence are critical to ongoing success. Reporting to senior management, the Environmental and Compliance Officer will play a key role in ensuring the site operates in accordance with EPA licence conditions, development approvals, environmental legislation and WHS requirements.
This is a hands on, site based position suited to someone who enjoys being close to operations, identifying risks before they become issues, and working collaboratively with teams to maintain high standards of environmental and safety performance. You will have the opportunity to influence real outcomes, strengthen systems and help maintain the organisation's licence to operate.
  
What you will be doing:
  
This is a diverse role with broad responsibility across environmental compliance, risk management and workplace safety, including:
  
  • Managing compliance with NSW EPA Environment Protection Licence (EPL) conditions and requirements
  • Maintaining compliance registers, monitoring obligations and ensuring key actions are completed on time
  • Monitoring environmental risks including waste handling, stockpiling, water management, dust, odour, noise, litter and air quality
  • Coordinating EPA reporting, inspections, audits, notifications and regulatory correspondence
  • Investigating environmental incidents, non-compliances and corrective actions
  • Conducting site inspections and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement
  • Reviewing environmental performance data and implementing corrective actions where required
  • Monitoring waste acceptance processes and ensuring compliance with approved waste categories
  
About you
  • You are a practical and detail focused environmental professional who enjoys working within an operational environment and being visible on site.
  • You understand how to balance regulatory obligations with operational realities and are confident interpreting environmental requirements and translating them into practical actions. You build credibility with operational teams, communicate effectively at all levels and take a proactive approach to identifying and managing risk.
  • Most importantly, you are someone who enjoys ownership, values accountability, and wants to make a genuine contribution to environmental and safety performance.
  
What you will bring

  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or equivalent
  • Approximately 3 to 5 years of experience in environmental compliance, WHS or operational environmental roles
  • Experience interpreting environmental approvals, licence conditions and regulatory requirements
  • Strong capability in inspections, risk assessments, compliance monitoring and documentation
  • Experience managing environmental incidents, investigations and corrective actions
  • Confidence engaging with regulators, consultants and operational stakeholders
  • Strong written communication and reporting skills
  
  
Why Join?

Domino’s Pizza Enterprises is one of the world's largest and most recognised quick service restaurant (QSR) brands, operating across multiple international markets and serving millions of customers every week.

The organisation is entering a new phase, including the appointment of a new Group CEO. With a focus on growth, innovation and operational improvement, Domino’s is continuing to invest in the systems, capability and leadership needed to support its next stage.

Safety is an important part of this work. With a large network of stores, delivery drivers and operational teams, there are a range of safety challenges to manage across different countries and operating environments.

This is an opportunity to join Domino’s Pizza Enterprises in a newly created Group Safety Lead role, working across 12 countries and a large, diverse operational network.

The role will suit a safety professional who is ready to broaden their experience and take on greater responsibility across a large international organisation. You will work closely with senior leaders and safety teams across different markets, helping to develop consistent approaches to safety, improve reporting and governance, and share good practice across the business.

Reporting initially to the Group CEO, the Group Safety Lead will provide safety leadership and subject matter expertise across 12 countries, including Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe.

You will work with local safety and operational teams to help develop the Group Safety Strategy, improve governance and reporting, and support a more consistent approach to managing risk.

The role will cover areas including delivery and road safety, fleet and driver risk, safety capability, risk management, reporting and sharing better ways of working across the organisation.

You won't be expected to do this through a large team. Much of the role will involve working with people across the business, building relationships, providing practical advice and helping local teams identify opportunities to improve.

This is a good opportunity for someone who enjoys working with operational teams and wants to gain broader experience across a complex, international organisation.

You will have a background in health and safety and be comfortable working with operational leaders and teams. You may currently be working as a Safety Manager, Senior Safety Advisor, HSE Business Partner or in a similar role and be looking for an opportunity to take the next step.

You will be someone who can build relationships, communicate clearly and turn safety requirements into practical solutions. You don't need to have worked in a global organisation before, but experience across multiple sites, jurisdictions or operational environments would be useful.

Experience in QSR, retail, transport, logistics, franchising, consumer services, aviation, infrastructure or other operationally intensive environments would be relevant. Exposure to road, driver, rider or fleet safety would also be well regarded.

Most importantly, you will be curious, practical and comfortable working with different people and perspectives. You will enjoy being part of a business where you can see the impact of your work and continue developing your own leadership capability.
